'''Matthew Dean Foreman'''  is an American mathematician at
[[University of California, Irvine]]. He has made notable contributions in [[set theory]] and in [[ergodic theory]].

==Biography==

Born in [[Los Alamos, New Mexico]], Foreman earned his [[Ph.D.]] from the
University of California, Berkeley in 1980 under [[Robert M. Solovay]]. His
dissertation title was ''Large Cardinals and Strong Model Theoretic Transfer Properties''.<ref>{{cite journal|jstor=1998706|title=Large Cardinals and Strong Model Theoretic Transfer Properties|last1=Foreman|first1=Matthew|journal=Transactions of the American Mathematical Society|year=1982|volume=272|issue=2|pages=427–463|doi=10.1090/S0002-9947-1982-0662045-X|doi-access=free}}</ref>

In addition to his mathematical work, Foreman is an avid sailor.

He and his family sailed their sailboat ''Veritas'' (a [[C&C Yachts|built by C&C Yachts]]) from North America to Europe in 2000. From 2000&ndash;2008 they sailed Veritas to the Arctic, the [[Shetland Islands]], [[Scotland]], [[Ireland]], [[England]], [[France]], [[Spain]], [[North Africa]] and [[Italy]].

Notable high points were [[Fastnet Rock]], Irish and Celtic seas and many passages including the
[[Whirlpool|Maelstrom]], [[Stad (peninsula)|Stad]], [[Pentland Firth]], [[Loch Ness]], the Corryveckan and the Irish Sea.
Further south they sailed through the [[Chenal du Four]] and [[Raz de Sein]], across the [[Bay of Biscay]] and around [[Cape Finisterre]].  After entering [[Gibraltar]], Foreman and his family circumnavigated the Western Mediterranean. Some notable stops included: [[Barcelona]], [[Morocco]], [[Tunisia]], [[Sicily]], [[Naples]], [[Sardinia]] and [[Corsica]]. In 2009 Foreman, his son with guest members as crew, circumnavigated Newfoundland.<ref>Foreman, Zachary (2007) "Under Way", Cruising World Magazine, October 2007</ref>

Foreman has been recognized for his sailing by twice winning the Ullman Trophy.<ref>Tailwind, [[Balboa Yacht Club]] "Annual Awards", 2003, 2011</ref>

==Work==
Foreman began his career in set theory. His early work with [[W. Hugh Woodin|Hugh Woodin]] included showing that it is consistent that the generalized continuum hypothesis (see [[continuum hypothesis]]) fails at every infinite cardinal.<ref>{{cite journal
| last1=Foreman | first1=Matthew
| last2=Woodin | first2=W. Hugh | authorlink2=W. Hugh Woodin
| title=The generalized continuum hypothesis can fail everywhere
| journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]]
| series=Second Series
| volume=133
| date=1991
| issue=1
| pages=1&ndash;35
| doi=10.2307/2944324 | jstor=2944324}}</ref> In joint work with [[Menachem Magidor]] and [[Saharon Shelah]] he formulated [[Martin's maximum]], a provably maximal form of [[Martin's axiom]] and showed its consistency.<ref>{{cite journal
| last1=Foreman | first1=Matthew
| last2=Magidor | first2=Menachem | authorlink2=Menachem Magidor
| last3=Shelah | first3=Saharon | authorlink3=Saharon Shelah
| title=Martin's maximum, saturated ideals, and nonregular ultrafilters. I
| journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]]
| series=Second Series
| volume=127
| date=1988
| issue=1
| pages=1&ndash;47
| doi=10.2307/1971415
| jstor=1971415}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal
| last1=Foreman | first1=Matthew
| last2=Magidor | first2=Menachem | authorlink2=Menachem Magidor
| last3=Shelah | first3=Saharon | authorlink3=Saharon Shelah
| title=Martin's maximum, saturated ideals and nonregular ultrafilters. II
| journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]]
| series=Second Series
| volume=127
| date=1988
| issue=3
| pages=521&ndash;545
| doi=10.2307/2007004
| jstor=2007004}}</ref> Foreman's later work in set theory was primarily concerned with developing the consequences of generic large cardinal axioms.<ref>{{cite book
| last1=Foreman | first1=Matthew
| contribution=Ideals and generic elementary embeddings
| title=Handbook of Set Theory
| pages=885–1147
| publisher=Springer
| date=2010
| doi=10.1007/978-1-4020-5764-9_14 | doi-access=free}}</ref> He also worked on classical "Hungarian" [[Infinitary combinatorics|partition relations]], mostly with [[András Hajnal]].<ref>{{cite journal
| last1=Foreman | first1=Matthew
| last2=Hajnal | first2=András | authorlink2=András Hajnal
| title=A partition relation for successors of large cardinals
| journal=[[Mathematische Annalen]]
| volume=325
| date=2003
| issue=3
| pages=583–623
| doi=10.1007/s00208-002-0323-7 | doi-access=}}</ref>

In the late 1980s Foreman became interested in [[Measure (mathematics)|measure]] theory and [[ergodic theory]]. With [[Randall Dougherty]] he settled the [[Edward Marczewski|Marczewski]] problem (1930) by showing that there is a Banach–Tarski decomposition of the unit ball in which all pieces have the [[property of Baire]] (see [[Banach–Tarski paradox]]).<ref>{{cite journal
| last1=Dougherty | first1=Randall | authorlink1=Randall Dougherty
| last2=Foreman | first2=Matthew
| title=Banach–Tarski decompositions using sets with the property of Baire
| journal=Journal of the American Mathematical Society
| volume=7
| date=1994
| issue=1
| pages=75–124
| doi=10.1090/S0894-0347-1994-1227475-8 | doi-access=free}}</ref> A consequence is the existence of a decomposition of an open dense subset of the unit ball into disjoint open sets that can be rearranged by isometries to form two open dense subsets of the unit ball. With Friedrich Wehrung, Foreman showed that the [[Hahn–Banach theorem]] implied the existence of a non-Lebesgue measurable set, even in the absence of any other form of the [[axiom of choice]].<ref>{{cite journal
| last1=Foreman | first1=Matthew
| last2=Wehrung | first2=Friedrich
| title=The Hahn–Banach theorem implies the existence of a non-Lebesgue measurable set
| journal=Fundamenta Mathematicae
| volume=138
| date=1991
| issue=1
| pages=13–19
| doi=10.4064/fm-138-1-13-19 | doi-access=free}}</ref>

This naturally led to attempts to apply the tools of [[descriptive set theory]] to classification problems in [[ergodic theory]]. His first work in this direction, with Ferenc Beleznay,<ref>{{cite journal
| last1=Beleznay | first1=Ferenc
| last2=Foreman | first2=Matthew
| title=The collection of distal flows is not Borel
| journal=American Journal of Mathematics
| volume=117
| date=1995
| issue=1
| pages=203–239
| doi=10.2307/2375041
| jstor=2375041}}</ref> showed that classical collections were beyond the [[Borel hierarchy]] in complexity. This was followed shortly by a proof of the analogous results for measure-preserving transformations with generalized discrete spectrum. In a collaboration with [[Benjamin Weiss]]<ref>{{cite journal
| last1=Foreman | first1=Matthew
| last2=Weiss | first2=Benjamin | authorlink2=Benjamin Weiss
| title=An anti-classification theorem for ergodic measure-preserving transformations
| journal=[[Journal of the European Mathematical Society]]
| volume=6
| date=2004
| issue=3
| pages=277&ndash;292
| doi=10.4171/JEMS/10 | doi-access=free}}</ref> and [[Daniel Rudolph]]<ref name="Foreman Rudolph Weiss">{{cite journal | last1=Foreman | first1=Matthew | last2=Rudolph | first2=Daniel | last3=Weiss | first3=Benjamin | author-link2=Daniel Rudolph |author-link3=Benjamin Weiss |title=The conjugacy problem in ergodic theory | journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]] | series=Second Series | volume=173 | issue=3 | date=May 1, 2011 | issn=0003-486X | doi=10.4007/annals.2011.173.3.7 | pages=1529–1586| doi-access=free }}</ref> Foreman showed that no residual class of measure-preserving transformations can have algebraic invariants and that the isomorphism relation on ergodic measure-preserving transformations is not Borel. This negative result finished a program proposed by von Neumann in 1932.<ref>{{cite journal
| last1=von Neumann | first1=J. | authorlink1=John von Neumann
| title=Zur Operatorenmethode in der klassischen Mechanik
| journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]]
| series=Second Series
| volume=33
| issue=3
| pages=587–642
| date=1932
| doi=10.2307/1968537
| jstor=1968537}}</ref> This result was extended by Foreman and Weiss to show that smooth area-preserving diffeomorphisms of the 2-torus are unclassifiable.

Foreman's work in set theory continued during this period. He co-edited (with [[Akihiro Kanamori|Kanamori]]) the ''Handbook of Set Theory'' and showed that various combinatorial properties of ω<sub>2</sub> and ω<sub>3</sub> are equiconsistent with [[huge cardinal]]s.<ref>{{cite journal
| last1=Foreman | first1=Matthew
| title=Smoke and mirrors: combinatorial properties of small cardinals equiconsistent with huge cardinals
| journal=[[Advances in Mathematics]]
| volume=222
| date=2009
| issue=2
| pages=565&ndash;595
| doi=10.1016/j.aim.2009.05.006 | doi-access=free}}</ref>

==Recognition==
In 1998 Foreman was an Invited Speaker of the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Berlin.<ref>{{cite book
| last1=Foreman | first1=Matthew
| chapter=Generic large cardinals: New axioms for mathematics?
| title=Documenta Mathematica (Bielefeld), Extra Volume ICM Berlin
| date=1998
| volume=II
| pages=11–21
| chapter-url=https://www.elibm.org/ft/10011637000}}</ref>

In 2021, he gave the [[Gödel Lecture]] titled ''Gödel Diffeomorphisms.''

He was named to the 2023 class of Fellows of the [[American Mathematical Society]], "for contributions to axioms of mathematics, Banach-Tarski phenomena, and descriptive dynamical systems".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ams.org/cgi-bin/fellows/fellows_by_year.cgi|title=2023 Class of Fellows|publisher=American Mathematical Society|access-date=2022-11-09|archive-date=2022-11-09|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221109214706/https://www.ams.org/cgi-bin/fellows/fellows_by_year.cgi|url-status=dead}}</ref>
